newsitem.title: USA: U.S. June S&P 500s finish lower after rate hike.
newsitem.headline: U.S. June S&P 500s finish lower after rate hike.

text.p: U.S. June Standard and Poor's 500 futures ended lower after the Federal Reserve raised its federal funds target to 5.50 percent from 5.25 percent.
The Fed left the discount rate unchanged at 5.0 percent.
The Fed, after its policy meeting today, said it raised rates in light of "persisting strength" in U.S. demand, and called the tightening "a prudent step" to extend economic expansion.
June S&Ps' initial reaction to the Fed's announcement was delayed and the market stood virtually unmoved for several minutes after the news.

June then rallied to 806.00 before tumbling just as quickly to a session low of 794.75. The market later rallied above key 800.00 before sliding to a fresh session low at 794.50. June closed just above there, at 795.20, down 6.05 points.
Traders blamed late weakness on the notion that this tightening was likely the first in a cycle.
"I think these comments that basically the Fed doesn't do things in quarter-points means you open the door for additional moves," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader for DLJ in New York.
Several former Fed officials and Wall Street experts agreed that today's rate hike marks the beginning of a new tightening cycle. It was the Fed's first tightening move since February 1, 1995.
Hohmann and others said S&Ps could see sideways trade or consolidation on Wednesday as players regroup after today's wild ride.

Hohmann noted an uptrending support line in cash S&P 500s at 787.50. He said the market could find support from there, but also noted some technical disappointment that the market failed again above 800.00.
"It's too tight to tell right now," Hohmann said.
One S&P 500 futures trader said futures volume was brisk after the FOMC announcement, with aggressive flows on both sides of the market.
"It was a tough day for the longs," he said, adding that he was "perplexed" by the midafternoon bounce back above 800.00. He said 788.00 support would hold any dip below 790.00.
"I would expect us to go lower before getting back above 800.00," he said. He noted liquidity gaps from Monday's late rally at 792.60 to 789.70.
"We may test 788.00 and then consolidate," the S&P 500 futures trader said.
He said June S&P 500 futures volume was estimated at 62,000 contracts, a third of which was likely traded after the FOMC announcement.

At the close, Nasdaq 100s were 0.15 lower at 818.25, KCBT Value Line futures were down 6.70 points at 704.90, Nikkei 225 index futures rose 200.0 to 18,495 and Midcap 400s rose 0.75 points to 262.85. ((--Derivatives Desk: 312-408-8750)) email:derivatives@reuters.com
